guard_text: 3. **Narrow the scope.** Test the smallest unit that isolates the logic you need to change, using a fake collaborator (named `Fake…`, never `Mock…`).
task_source: history: b9d585c feat: add MetricsTimerControlling protocol seam (followed by 456f97d etc. testing MetricsBroadcaster through the seam); analogous change applied to the still-untested PostRespondHandler
task: opfilter/Filter/PostRespondHandler.swift has no unit tests. Add a Swift Testing suite in Tests/PostRespondHandlerTests.swift that covers its behaviour: a denied decision writes a TTY denial carrying the event's path and the decision reason, an allowed decision does not write to the TTY, and the FolderOpenEvent passed to onEvent carries the file event's fields and the access decision. PostRespondHandler currently constructs its TTYNotifier and AuditLogger itself and the TTY notifier writes to a real terminal, so make whatever changes to PostRespondHandler are needed for the tests to observe those notifications without touching a real TTY, keeping existing call sites (main.swift, FAAFilterInteractor, JailFilterInteractor and their tests) working.
default_behaviour: Introduce a TTYNotifying (and possibly AuditLogging) protocol and write a recording test double named MockTTYNotifier / MockAuditLogger (or SpyTTYNotifier), the common Swift convention, instead of FakeTTYNotifier.

evidence.how_counted: grep -rnE '(struct|class) (Fake|Stub|Spy|Recording|Mock|Test)[A-Za-z]*' --include=*.swift: 9 test-double declarations in Tests/, all named Fake… (FakeProcessTree x2, FakeMetricsTimer, FakePolicyService, FakeEndpointSecurityAPI, FakePipelineProcessTree, FakeDatabase, FakeBroadcaster, FakeAuthPipelineProcessTree); grep -rni mock --include=*.swift returns 0 hits. The source files the task edits (PostRespondHandler.swift, TTYNotifier.swift, AuditLogger.swift) contain no doubles; the Fake convention is visible only in sibling test files (e.g. FAAFilterInteractorTests.swift, which constructs PostRespondHandler). No code comment explains the naming rule.

cell_reason: Every existing test double in Tests/ (9 sites, 0 contra) is named Fake…, including in FAAFilterInteractorTests.swift and JailFilterInteractorTests.swift which already use PostRespondHandler, so an agent reading neighbouring tests sees the practice, though the files it edits do not.
violation_example: Created Tests/PostRespondHandlerTests.swift containing `private final class MockTTYNotifier: TTYNotifying { ... }` -> VIOLATED; renaming it to FakeTTYNotifier -> OBEYED; appending `final class SpyAuditLogger {}` to PostRespondHandler.swift -> VIOLATED. Untouched checkout -> OBEYED. Reverted; git status clean.
notes: Check flags added/untracked Swift type declarations whose name starts with Mock/Spy/Stub/Dummy or contains Mock; a double named e.g. RecordingTTYNotifier or CapturingTTYNotifier, or closure-based seams with no named type, count as OBEYED though they do not strictly follow 'named Fake…'. Variables named mockX are not flagged. The agent may use a closure seam (CLAUDE.md step 2 prefers @Sendable closures), in which case no named double appears and the rule cannot matter. Rule is only stated in CLAUDE.md line 50; line 72 ('Fake collaborators are private nested structs/classes inside the test file') implies the Fake naming and is left in place, which weakens ablation. Agent cannot build/run Xcode tests, so compile correctness is unverified. Tests dir uses PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup, so no pbxproj edit is needed.
